name: Cordiaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach project Cordia boissieri as a rough-leaved woody Boraginales member with large white salver/trumpet flowers, yellow throat and white-to-yellow drupe, while explicitly teaching the current family-circumscription disagreement.

taxonomy_scope.project_teaching_treatment: Narrow Boraginales treatment recognizing Cordiaceae, following modern phylogenetic/familial studies.
taxonomy_scope.backbone_conflict: Kew POWO 2026 currently stores Cordia boissieri and Cordia under Boraginaceae sensu lato. This project retains a Cordiaceae lesson because recent Boraginales phylogenies continue to recognize Cordiaceae as a distinct family.

project_scope.note: Cordia boissieri is an accepted species native from southern Texas to eastern Mexico.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the rough gray-green leaf and the huge white flower with a yellow throat, then confirm the fleshy pale drupe.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Shrub or small tree. Leaves simple, alternate, broadly ovate, thick and densely pubescent/rough to the touch.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Large showy white sympetalous flowers with 5 spreading/ruffled lobes and a conspicuous yellow throat, borne in terminal clusters.
family_diagnostics.fruit: White to yellow-green fleshy drupe, olive-like in shape but unrelated to true olives.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Rough broad leaf + large white 5-lobed trumpet flower with yellow throat + pale drupe = project Cordiaceae/Cordia boissieri.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: rough leaf macro → whole flower → fused corolla/yellow throat → fruit → Boraginaceae-vs-Cordiaceae family card → range card
visual_lesson.intro: Anacahuita is easy to recognize visually; the harder lesson is taxonomic. Its species name is stable, but botanists differ on whether Cordia sits in broad Boraginaceae or a separate Cordiaceae.

steps.title: 1 · Feel the leaf with your eyes
steps.look_for: Broad ovate gray-green leaf densely pubescent, giving a coarse/velvety surface.

steps.title: 2 · Find the yellow throat
steps.look_for: Large white fused corolla opening into five ruffled lobes with a bright yellow throat.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the most distinctive project flowers.

steps.title: 3 · Show the fused corolla tube
steps.look_for: Petal tissue united below into a salver/trumpet-shaped tube.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the showy flower to Boraginales architecture.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the flower to the pale drupe
steps.why_it_matters: Late-season confirmation and explanation of the 'Texas olive' common name.

steps.title: 5 · Teach the family-circumscription disagreement
steps.look_for: Project/modern narrow treatment: Cordiaceae. Kew POWO/APG broad treatment: Boraginaceae sensu lato.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents two reputable systems from appearing contradictory or erroneous.

steps.title: 6 · Keep the native range honest
steps.look_for: Native southern Texas to eastern Mexico; ornamental plantings farther north are outside its wild native range.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates species identity from local provenance.

comparisons.title: Cordiaceae vs Boraginaceae sensu stricto
comparisons.rule: The project uses the narrow-family Boraginales framework in which woody Cordia is Cordiaceae; Kew POWO currently folds it into broad Boraginaceae. This is a family-circumscription choice, not a disagreement about Cordia boissieri being an accepted species.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not 'correct' the project family to Boraginaceae merely because POWO uses a broad treatment. Cordiaceae is explicitly supported by modern Boraginales family classifications; preserve both systems in the learner.

genera.fast_cue: rough broad leaf + huge white yellow-throated flower + pale drupe

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted species; native range southern Texas to eastern Mexico.
Project follows a narrow modern Boraginales family concept; Kew POWO currently stores Cordia in broad Boraginaceae.
